name: Leh-Ladakh
description: Leh-Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert sitting between 3,000 and 5,600 metres, offering stark Himalayan landscapes, ancient Buddhist monasteries, and some of India's most demanding roads. It suits adventure travellers, photographers, and those seeking genuine remoteness, but the thin air demands acclimatisation and rules out the very young, very old, or anyone with cardiac or respiratory conditions without medical clearance.

attractions.name: Pangong Tso
attractions.description: A narrow, 134 km-long glacial lake at 4,350 m straddling the India-China border, famous for its water shifting through improbable shades of blue and green through the day. The 5-hour drive from Leh over Chang La pass is demanding, and the lake shore itself offers little shelter from wind and cold.

attractions.name: Nubra Valley & Hunder Sand Dunes
attractions.description: A broad river valley north of Leh accessed over the Khardung La pass (~5,359 m), home to cold-desert sand dunes at Hunder and the rare double-humped Bactrian camels. The valley is lush relative to Leh and gives a very different landscape within a single trip.

attractions.name: Diskit Monastery
attractions.description: The oldest and largest monastery in Nubra Valley, founded in the 14th century and perched on a rocky spur with commanding views over the valley floor. The 32-metre Maitreya Buddha statue erected in 2010 is a striking modern addition visible from kilometres away.

attractions.name: Thiksey Monastery
attractions.description: A 12-storey monastery complex 19 km east of Leh, often compared to the Potala Palace in Lhasa for its tiered white-and-ochre architecture. The morning prayer ceremony at 6:30 am is open to visitors and is one of the most authentic monastic experiences in Ladakh.

attractions.name: Hemis Monastery
attractions.description: The wealthiest and best-known Drukpa Kagyu monastery in Ladakh, 45 km south-east of Leh, housing a substantial collection of thangkas, statues, and relics. The annual Hemis Festival (usually June-July) features masked Cham dances and draws large crowds.

attractions.name: Magnetic Hill
attractions.description: A stretch of road 30 km west of Leh where an optical illusion created by the surrounding terrain makes vehicles appear to roll uphill when left in neutral. The phenomenon itself takes only minutes to experience; it is a brief roadside stop rather than a destination in its own right.

attractions.name: Shanti Stupa
attractions.description: A white-domed Buddhist stupa built in 1991 on a hilltop above Chanspa, Leh, at around 3,620 m, offering a 360-degree panorama over the Leh Valley and the Stok Kangri range. The 500-step climb from the road is manageable for most healthy visitors after acclimatisation.

attractions.name: Leh Palace
attractions.description: A 17th-century nine-storey royal palace modelled after the Potala Palace, dominating the old town of Leh. Much of the interior is in decay and the ASI-managed restoration is ongoing, but the rooftop views over Leh and the Indus Valley are excellent.

attractions.name: Tso Moriri
attractions.description: A remote high-altitude lake at 4,522 m in the Changthang plateau, roughly 240 km south-east of Leh via Chumathang, far less visited than Pangong Tso and genuinely wild. It is a Ramsar-designated wetland and breeding ground for the bar-headed goose and black-necked crane; overnight permit and restricted camping apply.

attractions.name: Alchi Monastery
attractions.description: A cluster of small 11th-12th century temples 70 km west of Leh, built by the translator Rinchen Zangpo, containing some of the finest and best-preserved Kashmir-style wall murals and stucco sculptures in any Himalayan monastery. Unlike most Ladakhi gompas it sits on flat ground at river level, making it genuinely accessible to seniors.
